T h is appeal coming on for hearing this day, t h e cou rt pa  following:
 ORDER 1.Being aggrieved by the award dated 27th February, 2015 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena, in Claim Case No.331/2013, appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal for enhancement.

2.In brief, facts of the case are that husband of appellant No.1, father of appellants No.2 to 4 and son of appellant No.5, namely Kamal Singh aged 24 years, was coming to Gwalior from Haridwar by taking Kawar by the side of road and as soon as he reached in the territorial limits of police Station Arniya Khurja, Distt. Bulandshahar, respondent No.2/driver of truck No.HR42/D- 02777, which was owned by respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.3, by driving the said truck rashly &
negligently dashed Kamalsingh along with Atar Singh & others and due to the injuries suffered Kamalsingh & Atar Singh died & others suffered injuries.
On the report, crime No.127/2013 was registered under Section 279, 337, 338, 304-A of IPC at police Station Arniya Khurja.
During investigation, dead-body Panchnama was prepared and 04:45:01 PM postmortem was conducted.
Injured were medically examined.
Offending truck was seized from respondent No.2.
After investigation, charge-sheet was filed.
3.The dependents of deceased filed a claim for a sum of Rs.49,15,000/- by mentioning that deceased was a mason and used to do work of tiles fitting and used to earn a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
The learned Claims Tribunal by assessing his income as Rs.3,000/- on notional basis, awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,41,000/-.
The claimants being dissatisfied with the said award have filed this Misc. Appeal for enhancement.
4.Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that learned Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased to be Rs.3,000/- per month which is on very lower side.
Deceased Kamal Singh was a skilled mason, therefore, as per the Minimum Wages Act, his income should have been assessed as Rs.5,550/- per month.

Beside that, in the light of the decision of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi as reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680 the claimants Mahila Lakshmi Devi vs Kuldeep Kumar on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147659536/

sentences.text: 7.The appellants/claimants have not challenged the award passed by learned Claims Tribunal on issues No.1 to 3, hence, the conclusion drawn by learned Claims Tribunal over issues No.1 to 3 needs no interference.

8.So far as income of deceased Kamalsingh is concerned, it is stated by Laxmidevi (AW-1) and Bharat Singh (AW-3) that deceased Kamalsingh was doing the job of marble/tiles fitting whereby he was earning Rs.15,000/- / 16,000/- per month, but neither any documentary nor any cogent evidence in this regard is on record.

If the deceased was doing the work of marble/tiles fitting and thereby earning Rs.15,000/- / 16,000/- per month, bank pass-book of the deceased and any other document regarding earning such amount could be filed, but such important evidence could not be adduced on behalf of the appellants.
It is settled principle of law that mere assertion in regard to the income of the deceased is not sufficient.
Cogent and reliable evidence to prove the income of the deceased is necessary in claim cases.
In this regard, the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Syed Basheer Ahamed and others vs. Mohammed Jameel and another, (2009) 2 SCC 225 is referable.

sentences.text:
The relevant paras 14 and 21 of that judgment in this regard are as infra:
"14.Similarly

, although the Act is a beneficial legislation, it can neither be allowed to be used as a source of profit, nor as a windfall to the persons affected nor should it be punitive to the person(s) liable to pay compensation.
The determination of compensation must be based on certain data, establishing reasonable nexus between the loss incurred by the dependants of the deceased and the compensation to be awarded to them.
In a nutshell, the amount of compensation determined to be payable to the claimant(s) has to be fair and reasonable by accepted legal standards.
21.In the instant case, the main grievance of the appellant is that the High Court erred in reducing the monthly income of the deceased from Rs 7000 to Rs 4000.
More so, when the claim of the appellants was that the deceased was earning about Rs 20,000 per month.
It needs little emphasis that insofar as the SOODAN PRASAD on the claimants to prove this fact by leading reliable and 04:45:01 PM cogent evidence before the Tribunal.
A bare assertion in the claim petition in that behalf is not sufficient to discharge that onus."

9.Though the employment of the deceased as mason or his work of marble/tiles fitting was not found proved, yet keeping in view guidelines of State Legal Services Authority, it would be in the fitness of things to assume the income of the deceased as Rs.5,270/- per month which was the Mahila Lakshmi Devi vs Kuldeep Kumar on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147659536/

sentences.text: One of these heads is loss of consortium.

In legal parlance, "consortium"
is a compendious term which encompasses "spousal consortium", "parental consortium", and "filial consortium".

The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, Signed by: MADHU comfort,
guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which SOODAN PRASAD Signing time: 19-12-2023 is a loss to his family.

With respect to a spouse, it would 04:45:01 PM include sexual relations with the deceased spouse : [Rajesh v.
Rajbir Singh, (2013) 9 SCC 54 : (2013) 4 SCC (Civ) 179 :
(2013) 3 SCC (Cri) 817 : (2014) 1 SCC (L&S) 149]

sentences.text:
Spousal consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband-wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of "company, society, cooperation,
affection, and aid of the other in every conjugal relation".
[Black's Law Dictionary(5th Edn., 1979).
] Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training".
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their role in the family unit.
Consortium is a special prism reflecting changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationships.
Modern jurisdictions world-over have recognised that the value of a child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in the case of the death of a child.
Most jurisdictions therefore permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.
The amount awarded to the parents is a compensation for loss of the love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child.

sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of filial consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.

A few High Courts have awarded compensation on this count [ Rajasthan High Court in Jagmala Ram v.Sohi Ram, 2017 SCC OnLine Raj 3848 : (2017) 4 RLW 3368; Uttarakhand High Court in Rita Rana v.
